Definition: Thalamocortical fibers from the medial geniculate nucleus to the primary auditory cortex (Heschl gyrus); also called auditory radiation
synonyms: Acoustic radiations ; Acoustic radiations structure ; Auditory radiations ; Fibrae geniculotemporales ; Geniculotemporal tract ; Radiatio acustica

Definition: Myelinated nerve fibers passing transversely through the lamina terminalis and connecting symmetrically corresponding parts of the two cerebral hemispheres; connects olfactory bulbs, anterior perforated substance, and temporal lobes across the midline
synonyms: Anterior commissure ; Structure of anterior commissure ; commissure anterior

Definition: Thalamocortical fibers connecting the anterior and mediodorsal thalamic nuclei with the prefrontal and cingulate cortex
A curved bundle connecting temporal and frontal cortex; now considered a subdivision of the superior longitudinal fasciculus connecting Wernicke area to Broca area
Occipital forceps; callosal fibers connecting the two occipital lobes through the splenium of the corpus callosum
synonyms: Forceps major ; Occipital radiation of corpus callosum ; Posterior forceps ; Structure of forceps major

Definition: Frontal forceps; callosal fibers connecting the two frontal lobes through the genu of the corpus callosum
synonyms: Anterior forceps ; Forceps minor ; Parietal radiation of corpus callosum ; Structure of forceps minor

Definition: Long C-shaped association bundle running adjacent to the cingulate gyrus; includes dorsal (cingulate) and ventral (hippocampal) components
synonyms: Cingulate fasciculus ; Cingulum ; Structure of cerebral cingulum ; Structure of cingulum

Definition: Dorsal division of the cingulum bundle (TRACULA convention); corresponds to the cingulate component
Ventral division of the cingulum bundle (TRACULA convention); corresponds to the hippocampal/parahippocampal component
Dorsal component of the cingulum bundle running adjacent to the cingulate gyrus
Ventral component of the cingulum bundle connecting parahippocampal gyrus to cingulate cortex

The ventral-most component of the cingulum bundle curving around the genu of the corpus callosum and extending posteriorly against the subgenual cingulate cortex; carries fibers connecting orbitofrontal and subgenual cingulate cortex with the amygdala, hippocampus and thalamus. A primary target of deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant major depressive disorder (Mayberg subcallosal cingulate target). Described as a distinct subdivision by Heilbronner and Haber (2014) and Bullock et al. (2022).

The peri-genual subsection of the cingulum bundle curving around the genu of the corpus callosum; connects the subgenual and anterior cingulate cortex with the orbitofrontal cortex and anterior thalamic nuclei. Defined as a distinct subdivision in the XTRACT atlas (Warrington et al. 2020). Overlaps anatomically with the subgenual cingulum; XTRACT defines the boundary by waypoint ROIs at the level of the genu.

The temporal subsection of the cingulum bundle running along the parahippocampal gyrus into the temporal lobe; connects posterior cingulate and retrosplenial cortex with the temporal pole, entorhinal cortex, and perirhinal cortex. Defined as a distinct subdivision in the XTRACT atlas (Warrington et al. 2020). Distinguished from the ventral/hippocampal cingulum by its more anterior temporal termination pattern.

The largest commissural white matter structure of the brain, connecting homologous and heterologous regions of the left and right cerebral hemispheres via approximately 200-300 million myelinated axons; subdivided from anterior to posterior into the rostrum, genu, body, isthmus, and splenium.
Anterior portion of the corpus callosum body at the level of the primary motor cortex
Central segment of the corpus callosum body
Parietal segment of the corpus callosum body
Prefrontal segment of the corpus callosum body
Premotor segment of the corpus callosum body
Temporal segment of the corpus callosum body
The anterior, rostral bend of the corpus callosum connecting the two prefrontal cortices
The narrow portion of the corpus callosum between the body and splenium; connects superior temporal and posterior parietal areas
Posterior portion of the corpus callosum body at the level of the primary somatosensory cortex
Rostral body of the corpus callosum at the level of the premotor and supplementary motor cortex
The most anterior and ventral portion of the corpus callosum; connects orbitofrontal regions
The posterior bulbous end of the corpus callosum connecting the occipital and posterior parietal lobes; carries visual callosal fibers
Fibers from cortex projecting to the pontine nuclei via the cerebral peduncle; includes frontal (FPT) and parieto-occipital (POPT) components
Projection fibers from layer V pyramidal cells of the motor cortex descending through the internal capsule; decussate at the medullary pyramids to control contralateral voluntary movement
Fibers from motor, premotor, prefrontal and other cortical areas projecting to the caudate nucleus and putamen
Cerebellar efferent pathway from the dentate nucleus crossing to the contralateral red nucleus and ventral lateral thalamus; involved in motor coordination
White matter lateral to the claustrum and medial to the insula; contains short and long association fibers connecting frontal and temporal lobes
The major efferent tract of the hippocampus, arching from the hippocampus under the corpus callosum to the mammillary bodies and septal nuclei

A ICBM-DTI-81 atlas label covering fibers of the fimbria-fornix and stria terminalis that cannot be resolved as separate structures at standard DTI resolution. The stria terminalis runs along the medial aspect of the caudate nucleus carrying amygdalofugal fibers to the hypothalamus and bed nucleus of the stria terminalis. Labeled as a combined entry in ICBM-DTI-81 because both structures share the same spatial volume at 1-2mm isotropic resolution.
Short association tract connecting the supplementary motor area and presupplementary motor area with the inferior frontal gyrus; involved in speech initiation and verbal fluency
Carries afferents to the cerebellum from the spinal cord (spinocerebellar) and brainstem (olivocerebellar); also contains efferent fibers
Long association bundle passing through the external/extreme capsule connecting frontal lobe with occipital and posterior temporal cortex; runs ventral to the uncinate fasciculus
source: AFQ ; ICBM-DTI-81 ; JHU_Tractography ; Bullock_2022 ; Pestilli_Brainlife ; XTRACT

Definition: Long association bundle along the lateral temporal and occipital lobes connecting occipital cortex with the temporal pole and amygdala
source: AFQ ; ICBM-DTI-81 ; JHU_Tractography ; Bullock_2022 ; Pestilli_Brainlife ; XTRACT

Definition: Large paired white matter structure positioned between the caudate nucleus and thalamus medially and the lentiform nucleus laterally; carries all ascending and descending projection fibers between the cerebral cortex and subcortical structures including the thalamus, brainstem and spinal cord. Divided into the anterior limb, genu, and posterior limb, with retrolenticular and sublenticular extensions.

The anterior subdivision of the internal capsule lying between the head of the caudate nucleus and the anterior lentiform nucleus; carries frontopontine fibers, corticostriatal fibers, and the anterior thalamic radiation connecting mediodorsal and anterior thalamic nuclei with prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex. A major target for deep brain stimulation and capsulotomy in treatment-resistant OCD and depression.

The posterior subdivision of the internal capsule lying between the thalamus and the posterior lentiform nucleus; carries the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts, superior thalamic radiation, and parietopontine and temporopontine fibers. Damage produces contralateral hemiplegia; the posterior limb is the most clinically critical segment of the internal capsule.

The portion of the internal capsule posterior to the lentiform nucleus; carries the posterior thalamic radiation including the optic radiation from the lateral geniculate nucleus, and parietopontine and occipito-pontine fibers. Damage produces contralateral hemianopia.
A complex bundle of fibers connecting the olfactory regions, hypothalamus, and midbrain; includes dopaminergic projections of the reward system
Sensory pathway carrying discriminative touch and proprioception from the contralateral body; ascends through the brainstem to the thalamus
synonyms: Lemniscus medialis ; Medial lemniscus ; Medial lemniscus structure

Definition: The largest cerebellar peduncle; carries pontocerebellar fibers from the contralateral pontine nuclei to the cerebellar cortex
Association bundle connecting the superior temporal gyrus with the parietal lobe; involved in auditory and language processing

Label_uberon: medial longitudinal fasciculus of the pons
Definition: Paired longitudinal brainstem tracts running near the midline through all three brainstem segments; composed of ascending and descending fibers coordinating conjugate eye movements via connections between the oculomotor, trochlear, and abducens nuclei. The main intersegmental tract of the brainstem. Lesions produce internuclear ophthalmoplegia, commonly seen in multiple sclerosis.

The angular gyrus subdivision of the middle longitudinal fasciculus; connects the superior temporal gyrus with the inferior parietal lobule (angular gyrus). Identified as a distinct component in Bullock et al. 2019 and Makris et al. 2013. Corresponds to the inferior parietal termination consistent with monkey tract-tracing data.

The superior parietal lobule subdivision of the middle longitudinal fasciculus; connects the superior temporal gyrus with the superior parietal lobule. Described in Bullock et al. 2019 and Makris et al. 2013. This component is debated: monkey tract-tracing does not show strong superior temporal to superior parietal connectivity, raising the possibility of a human-specific pathway or tractography false positive.
Geniculocalcarine tract carrying visual information from the lateral geniculate nucleus to the primary visual cortex; includes Meyer loop (lower visual field) inferolaterally through temporal lobe
synonyms: Geniculocalcarine tract ; Optic radiation ; Structure of optic radiation

Definition: Corticopontine fibers from parietal and occipital cortex projecting to the pontine nuclei via the posterior limb of the internal capsule
The posterior segment of the arcuate fasciculus connecting posterior superior temporal gyrus with inferior parietal lobule
Reticulospinal fibers from the reticular formation of the brainstem descending to the spinal cord; modulates muscle tone and autonomic functions
Corticostriatal fibers between orbitofrontal cortex and striatum
Corticostriatal fibers between occipital cortex and striatum
Corticostriatal fibers between parietal cortex and striatum
Corticostriatal fibers between somatosensory cortex and striatum
Corticostriatal fibers between primary motor cortex and striatum
Corticostriatal fibers between prefrontal cortex and striatum
Corticostriatal fibers between premotor cortex and striatum
Primary efferent pathway of the cerebellum; carries dentate nucleus output to the contralateral red nucleus and thalamus
Large association bundle in the dorsolateral white matter connecting frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes; contains the arcuate fasciculus and subdivides into SLF I-III
Dorsomedial SLF subdivision connecting precuneus and superior parietal lobule with supplementary motor area and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex
Middle SLF subdivision connecting angular gyrus with dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
Ventral SLF subdivision in the frontal and parietal operculum connecting supramarginal gyrus with inferior frontal gyrus
Thalamocortical fibers connecting the ventral posterior thalamic nucleus with the primary somatosensory cortex

clean_label: temporo-parietal connection to superior parietal lobule
Definition: Association fibers connecting superior temporal cortex with the superior parietal lobule
Thalamocortical fibers connecting the pulvinar with occipital cortex
Thalamocortical fibers connecting pulvinar and LP nucleus with posterior parietal cortex
Thalamocortical fibers connecting ventral posterior thalamic nucleus with primary somatosensory cortex
Thalamocortical fibers connecting ventral lateral thalamic nucleus with primary motor cortex
Thalamocortical fibers connecting mediodorsal and anterior thalamic nuclei with prefrontal cortex
Thalamocortical fibers connecting ventral lateral thalamic nucleus with premotor cortex
Hook-shaped association bundle connecting the anterior temporal lobe and amygdala with the orbitofrontal cortex via the limen insulae
Efferent pathway from the amygdala projecting to the hypothalamus, thalamus, and basal forebrain; part of the limbic system
Short association tract connecting dorsal and ventral occipital cortex running perpendicular to the calcarine sulcus; described by Wernicke (1881)
synonyms: Perpendicular fasciculus ; Structure of vertical occipital fasciculus ; Vertical occipital fasciculus

Definition: Transverse pontine fibers crossing the midline within the middle cerebellar peduncle; these fibers originate from the pontine nuclei and project to the contralateral cerebellum. In DTI they are identifiable as the decussating component of the MCP and cannot be fully separated from the surrounding peduncle at standard resolution.

The central, largest portion of the corpus callosum between the genu and splenium; fibers pass laterally through the corona radiata to connect frontal, parietal and temporal cortices of the two hemispheres. No single UBERON or SNOMED term maps to this undivided body as a distinct ontology class; this label represents the ICBM-DTI-81 atlas parcellation unit.

Paired structures at the base of the midbrain formed by corticospinal, corticobulbar and corticopontine fibers descending from the internal capsule; each peduncle consists of the crus cerebri anteriorly and the tegmentum posteriorly.

Fan-shaped mass of white matter fibers that radiate from the internal capsule to all parts of the cerebral cortex; represents the superior continuation of the internal capsule where the projection fibers spread out. Divided by convention into anterior, superior, and posterior subdivisions at the level of the corpus callosum genu and splenium.

The anterior subdivision of the corona radiata containing thalamocortical and corticothalamic fibers connecting the anterior thalamic nucleus and mediodorsal thalamic nucleus with the prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex; bounded posteriorly at the level of the posterior edge of the genu of the corpus callosum.

The superior subdivision of the corona radiata comprising projection fibers between the motor and sensory cortices and the thalamus; bounded anteriorly at the posterior edge of the genu and posteriorly at the anterior edge of the splenium of the corpus callosum.

The posterior subdivision of the corona radiata containing fibers from the posterior parietal and occipital cortices projecting to and from the posterior thalamus; overlaps spatially with the superior longitudinal fasciculus and posterior thalamic radiation at its margins.

Thalamocortical fibers connecting the posterior thalamus (pulvinar, lateral geniculate nucleus) with the parietal, occipital and posterior temporal cortices; includes the optic radiation as its ventral component. In the ICBM-DTI-81 atlas this label explicitly encompasses the optic radiation.

A sheet of white matter in the temporal and occipital lobes containing the inferior longitudinal fasciculus and inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus running in parallel; in the ICBM-DTI-81 atlas this label bundles both tracts together as they cannot be resolved separately at standard DTI resolution.

A sheet of white matter lateral to the putamen and medial to the claustrum; contains cortical association fibers including components of the inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus and uncinate fasciculus passing between frontal and temporal lobes.
synonyms: External capsule ; Structure of external capsule

Definition: White matter bundle running dorsal to the caudate nucleus and curving around its upper edge; carries corticostriatal fibers primarily from dorsal prefrontal, anterior cingulate, and association cortices to the caudate nucleus. Distinguished from the external capsule in that Muratoff's bundle fibers more commonly terminate in the caudate whereas external capsule fibers more commonly terminate in the putamen. Discussed in Bullock et al. 2022 as distinct from the external capsule and superior fronto-occipital fasciculus.

A white matter bundle running along the dorsomedial margin of the internal capsule connecting frontal lobe with posterior cortical areas; its anatomical independence from the anterior limb of the internal capsule is debated, and in the ICBM-DTI-81 atlas it is explicitly noted as possibly representing part of the anterior internal capsule rather than a distinct fasciculus.

Callosal fibers from the body and splenium of the corpus callosum that sweep laterally to form the roof and lateral walls of the occipital and temporal horns of the lateral ventricles; lies immediately adjacent to the ependyma of the ventricle.

The temporal component of the superior longitudinal fasciculus connecting posterior superior temporal gyrus and angular gyrus with inferior frontal and prefrontal cortex; corresponds to the arcuate fasciculus in many classification schemes. Identified as a distinct probabilistic label in the JHU White Matter Tractography Atlas.
